title: The Look of Love
original_issue: Verve (album The Look of Love, 18 Sep 2001)
personnel: Diana Krall (vocals, piano); Claus Ogerman (orchestra arrangement, conductor); Tommy LiPuma (producer). The album credits also list Christian McBride (bass), Jeff Hamilton and Peter Erskine (drums), Russell Malone, John Pisano and Romero Lubambo (guitars), Paulinho da Costa and Luis Conte (percussion), not assigned by track in the source
trivia: Burt Bacharach wrote the tune for the 1967 spoof Casino Royale, where Dusty Springfield sang it and it earned an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song. Krall's 2001 version, with strings arranged and conducted by Claus Ogerman, comes from the album that became her first to top the Canadian Albums Chart and won her a Juno for Album of the Year.

track.title: The Look of Love
track.query: Diana Krall The Look of Love 2001

notes: Wikipedia gives two album session blocks, 9 to 11 March 2001 (Avatar, New York) and 3 to 4 June 2001 (Abbey Road, London and Capitol, Hollywood), and does not say which holds the title track, so only the year is recorded. Personnel is the album credit list, not assigned by track.

title: Why Was I Born?
original_issue: Milestone (live album Without a Song: The 9/11 Concert, 30 Aug 2005)
personnel: Sonny Rollins (tenor saxophone); Clifton Anderson (trombone); Stephen Scott (piano); Bob Cranshaw (electric bass); Perry Wilson (drums); Kimati Dinizulu (percussion)
trivia: Rollins heard the World Trade Center collapse from his apartment a few blocks away and left with only his saxophone, then played this Berklee Performance Center concert in Boston four days later. His solo on this 1929 Jerome Kern tune won the 2006 Grammy Award for Jazz Instrumental Solo, and the concert reached release four years after it was played.

track.title: Why Was I Born?
track.query: Sonny Rollins Why Was I Born Without a Song The 9/11 Concert 2001
track.notes: live track (16:14) from the Berklee Performance Center, Boston

notes: GAP: recorded 2001, first released 2005 (4 yrs). The album page dates the whole concert to 15 September 2001. Chosen over the title track Without a Song because this is the performance that won the Grammy.

title: Footprints
original_issue: Verve (live album Footprints Live!, 2002)
personnel: Wayne Shorter (tenor and soprano saxophones); Danilo Perez (piano); John Patitucci (bass); Brian Blade (drums)
trivia: This was the first album to feature Shorter's Footprints Quartet with Danilo Perez, John Patitucci and Brian Blade, and the first official live album under his own name. It was recorded at the Festival de Jazz de Vitoria-Gasteiz in Spain on 20 July 2001, and one reviewer pointed out a Rock-A-Bye Baby quote in the title track.

track.title: Footprints
track.query: Wayne Shorter Quartet Footprints Footprints Live 2001

notes: The album page assigns this track to the Vitoria-Gasteiz concert of 20 July 2001. Shorter plays tenor and soprano saxophones on this track. A live remake of his own 1966 tune; no earlier Footprints is in the set.

title: Paranoid Android
original_issue: Warner Bros. (album Largo, 13 Aug 2002)
personnel: Brad Mehldau (piano, vibes, prepared piano); Darek Oleszkiewicz (bass); Matt Chamberlain (drums, percussion, tabla); Jim Keltner (drums, snare drum, vibraphone); Jon Brion (guitar synthesizer, guitar treatments, percussion; producer)
trivia: Largo was produced by Jon Brion and recorded in April 2001 at Capitol Studio B in Hollywood. On this cover of Radiohead's song from OK Computer, two drummers, Matt Chamberlain and Jim Keltner, join Brion's guitar synthesizer and the piano trio, and it runs just over nine minutes.

track.title: Paranoid Android
track.query: Brad Mehldau Paranoid Android Largo 2001

notes: The infobox gives album sessions of 2 to 8 April 2001 at Capitol Studio B; the album followed in August 2002. The song page credits the writing to Radiohead. A second Mehldau card, after Exit Music (For a Film) from 1998, which is also a Radiohead song.

title: Don't Know Why
original_issue: Blue Note (single, 28 Jan 2002; album Come Away with Me, 26 Feb 2002)
personnel: Norah Jones (vocals, piano); Jesse Harris (acoustic and electric guitar); Lee Alexander (bass); Dan Rieser (drums); Arif Mardin, Jay Newland and Norah Jones (producers)
trivia: Jesse Harris first put his song on a 1999 album, but it was Norah Jones's debut single in January 2002 and won Grammys for Record of the Year, Song of the Year and Best Female Pop Vocal Performance. Its parent album Come Away with Me, issued on Blue Note, has sold more than 27 million copies worldwide.

track.title: Don't Know Why
track.query: Norah Jones Don't Know Why Come Away with Me 2002
track.notes: album version (3:06), not the 3:05 single edit

notes: Wikipedia gives the whole album sessions as 20 Sep 2000 to Dec 2001 at Sorcerer Sound (New York) and Allaire (Shokan, New York) with no date for this track, and the single is 28 Jan 2002, so 2001 is used as the likely recording year. Tagged crossover: an acoustic-pop record on the Blue Note label rather than a jazz-musician record.

artist: Bebo Valdés and Diego El Cigala
title: Lágrimas negras
original_issue: Calle 54/BMG (album Lágrimas negras, 10 Mar 2003)
personnel: Bebo Valdés (piano); Diego el Cigala (vocals); Javier Colina (bass); Israel Porrina 'Piraña' (cajón); Paquito D'Rivera (alto saxophone); Tata Güines (congas); Pancho Terry (shekere); Changuito (timbales); Fernando Trueba and Javier Limón (producers)
trivia: Cuban pianist Bebo Valdés, described as one of the founders of Latin jazz, teamed with the Spanish flamenco singer Diego el Cigala on this fusion of Cuban rhythms and flamenco vocals, produced by Fernando Trueba and Javier Limón. Wikipedia counts the album among the seven Grammy wins credited to Valdés.

track.title: Lágrimas negras

Not tagged crossover because Valdés is described as a founder of Latin jazz, so this is a jazz-musician record.

title: Jazz Crimes
original_issue: Warner Bros. (album Elastic, 10 Sep 2002)
personnel: Joshua Redman (tenor saxophone); Sam Yahel (keyboards); Brian Blade (drums); Bashiri Johnson (tambourine, shaker)
trivia: Elastic was Redman's first full record with electric instruments after eight acoustic albums, cut with keyboardist Sam Yahel and drummer Brian Blade at Sear Sound in New York in March 2002. AllMusic's review said it leaned more toward pop and soul-funk than straight jazz.

track.title: Jazz Crimes
track.query: Joshua Redman Elastic Band Jazz Crimes Elastic 2002

notes: Jazz Crimes is track 2 of the album. Composer credit: Redman wrote everything on the album except Oumou, which is by Sam Yahel, per Wikipedia and a JazzTimes review. Personnel is the quartet credited for the album; the individual track credits are not itemised in the source used.

title: Hardgroove
original_issue: Verve (album Hard Groove, 20 May 2003, credited to the RH Factor)
personnel: Roy Hargrove (trumpet, arranger, producer); Jacques Schwarz-Bart (tenor saxophone); Keith Anderson (alto saxophone); Chalmers 'Spanky' Alford and Cornell Dupree (guitars); Bernard Wright and Bobby Sparks (keyboards, clavinet); Pino Palladino (bass); Reggie Washington (electric bass); Daniel Moreno (percussion); Jason Thomas (drums)
trivia: The album is a tribute to Hargrove's childhood love of hip hop, with guests including Common, Erykah Badu, Q-Tip and D'Angelo. The opening title track is credited to keyboardist Bernard Wright rather than to Hargrove.

track.title: Hardgroove

track.notes: album version (5:31); the track is spelled Hardgroove, the album Hard Groove

notes: The album page gives sessions from January to September 2002 at Electric Lady Studios (New York); no date for this track, so 2002. Personnel is taken from the album's track-number credits for track 1. A second Hargrove card (after Mambo for Roy, 1997).

title: All at Sea
original_issue: UCJ/Candid/Verve (album Twentysomething, 20 Oct 2003 in Europe, May 2004 in the US; lead single)
personnel: Jamie Cullum (vocals, piano); Stewart Levine (producer); no other players are credited in the sources used
trivia: Cullum's own tune was the lead single from Twentysomething, recorded in June and July 2003 at Mayfair Studios in London. The album sold 2.5 million copies, is described as the fastest-selling jazz album in chart history, and made him the country's highest-selling jazz artist of 2003.

title: Dance Me to the End of Love
original_issue: Rounder (album Careless Love, 14 Sep 2004)
personnel: Madeleine Peyroux (vocals, acoustic guitar); Dean Parks (guitars); Larry Goldings (piano, Wurlitzer, organ, celeste); David Piltch (double bass); Jay Bellerose (drums, percussion); Larry Klein (producer). Album credits, not assigned by track in the source
trivia: Peyroux opened her 2004 album Careless Love, produced by Larry Klein, with this Leonard Cohen song. The album ranked No. 3 on Billboard's 2005 year-end Top Jazz Albums chart and reached No. 1 on the Swedish jazz albums chart.

track.query: Madeleine Peyroux Dance Me to the End of Love Careless Love 2004

title: Aruarian Dance
original_issue: Victor Entertainment (album Samurai Champloo Music Record: Departure, 23 Jun 2004)
personnel: Nujabes (composer, producer); no instrumentalists are credited in the sources used
trivia: Director Shinichiro Watanabe wanted hip hop producers for Samurai Champloo rather than his Cowboy Bebop composer Yoko Kanno, and Nujabes was the first name that came to mind. Wikipedia calls this track an early example of lo-fi hip hop and says it spread virally on the internet.

title: Feeling Good
original_issue: 143/Reprise (single, 4 Apr 2005; album It's Time, 8 Feb 2005)
personnel: Michael Bublé (vocals); Randy Waldman (piano); Dean Parks (guitars); Brian Bromberg (bass); Vinnie Colaiuta (drums); Rafael Padilla (percussion); Neil Devor and Jochem van der Saag (programming); arranged by David Foster and Don Sebesky
trivia: Newley and Bricusse wrote the song for the 1964 stage musical The Roar of the Greasepaint - The Smell of the Crowd, and Nina Simone recorded it in 1965. Bublé's version opens his album It's Time, which topped the charts in Canada, Italy and Spain, and the track was used in ESPN's 2005 World Series of Poker coverage and the 2010 NBA draft broadcast.

personnel: Hiromi Uehara (piano); Tony Grey (bass); Martin Valihora (drums)
trivia: The Japanese pianist recorded this title track with bassist Tony Grey and drummer Martin Valihora at Blackbird Studio in Tennessee on 28 to 31 May 2005. NPR called the album part classical, part jazz and part simply unclassifiable.

track.title: Spiral
track.query: Hiromi Spiral Spiral 2005

title: How High the Moon
original_issue: Concord (album Good Night, and Good Luck, Music from and Inspired by the Motion Picture, 27 Sep 2005)
personnel: Dianne Reeves (vocals) with the combo of Peter Martin, Christoph Luty, Jeff Hamilton and Matt Catingub (instruments not assigned in the source used)
trivia: Reeves appears as a jazz singer in George Clooney's 2005 film about Edward R. Murrow and Senator Joseph McCarthy, and most of the jazz numbers were recorded live. The soundtrack album won the 2006 Grammy for Best Jazz Vocal Album, and this tune from the 1940 revue Two for the Show is on it.

personnel: Ornette Coleman (alto saxophone); Denardo Coleman (drums); Greg Cohen (bass); Tony Falanga (bass); Ornette Coleman and Michaela Deiss (producers)
trivia: Recorded live in Ludwigshafen, Germany, on 14 October 2005, Sound Grammar was Coleman's first new album in almost a decade and won the 2007 Pulitzer Prize for Music. Critics noted that his solo on this blues quotes the standard If I Loved You and Stephen Foster's Beautiful Dreamer.

trivia: Hancock's Joni Mitchell tribute won the 2008 Grammy for Album of the Year, only the third jazz album to do so after Mancini in 1959 and Getz/Gilberto in 1965, beating Kanye West, the Foo Fighters and Amy Winehouse. Norah Jones sings on this opening track.
